text:
Pittsburgh outplayed Dallas for most of the night and still needed a shootout to prove it. Connor Dewar's backhand, a 5 percent chance by the model, put the Penguins ahead less than two minutes into the third period. Then Tyler Seguin tipped in a Jason Robertson feed with 30 seconds left in regulation, a 9 percent chance, and the Stars had a point they had no clear claim to.

The numbers say PIT earned more. The Penguins held a 3.20 to 2.63 edge in expected goals, and at even strength it was 2.29 to 1.34. They attempted 68 shots to 54 and won 30 of 54 faceoffs. Across thousands of simulated replays of every shot, PIT wins 60 percent of the time. The Penguins dominated the first two periods, out-chancing the Stars 2.20 to 1.18, before Dallas flipped it in the third, 1.28 to 0.54. Even so, DAL's Jake Oettinger faced chances worth 3.20 goals and allowed one, saving 2.2 more than expected. Arturs Silovs matched him at the other end, 1.63 above expected.

The shootout was a trade of goals and saves until the end. Ben Kindel and Sidney Crosby scored for PIT, with Seguin and Wyatt Johnston answering for DAL. Rickard Rakell finished it after Robertson and Egor Chinakhov were stopped, and Mikko Rantanen's attempt was turned away to seal the 2-1 result. Dewar took first star, Silovs second. Seguin, the author of the late equalizer, was third.
